scopeNotes: New text needs independent review; earlier hashes do not certify it.
Map endpoints are not historical founding or extinction dates.
The imported map polygon covers 400 to 500 only. The narrative includes named sites from the broader region and later periods; their findings do not verify that polygon.
Alemannic identity is not treated as genetic uniformity or an unchanged tribe migrating together from one homeland. Early documentary labels are external.

Historical accounts differ in assigning individual battles to 496, 497 or 506 and in how they characterize ducal abolition in 732 versus the final suppression of resistance in 746. Phases are approximate and the ending describes a sequence, not a unique conquest date.

The 746 link targets frankish-kingdom, whose identity and 700 to 800 geometry were checked. It opens the receiving realm at the political event year; the imported boundaries themselves remain unverified.

Vörstetten’s display combines excavation-based reconstruction with borrowed furnishing models and practical visitor adaptations. None of the latter is presented as an original Vörstetten discovery. Orchard plants are not attributed to this site, where the museum says botanical evidence for orchards is lacking.

The bed belongs to Lauchheim-Mittelhofen grave 27. The flask and lyre belong to Trossingen grave 58. Their findspots and dates are kept separate. The lyre catalog gives manufacture around 560 while the burial is around 580; a room-plan label of 580 is not treated as manufacture.
The three museum object entries are kept under a combined 200-word paraphrase-and-note budget. No unavailable string material, musical repertoire or maker is invented.

The Niederstotzingen study’s primary results and discussion were read. Its overly definite background date for Clovis’s victory is not used against the historians’ disputed chronology. Genetic affinity does not assign ethnicity; the authors’ nonrepresentative-sample warning is retained.
Independent historical review, geometry assessment and depth certification remain pending.
